critique: The geological metaphor is conceptually rich but undermined by inconsistent visual hierarchy—the layer labels use geological terms (BEDROCK, LIMESTONE) yet the actual spending data presentation is conventionally flat, missing an opportunity to reinforce the depth metaphor through progressive visual density or stratification. The earth-tone palette successfully evokes sedimentary layers, but the interaction model contradicts the geological concept by allowing additions only to the surface rather than acknowledging how real geological processes involve compression and transformation of existing layers.
